payload.preflight_exit_code_diagnosed:
DIAGNOSED — closing my own observation from the 12:15Z tick. The non-zero exit is BY DESIGN and deterministic, not a fault. Full map read from scripts/agents-flow/cowork-tick-preflight.sh:

  SILENT        -> return 0
  WORK          -> return 1   (line 373)
  TOMBSTONED    -> return 1
  DEFER         -> return 1
  LOST_ELECTION -> return 1
  ERROR         -> return 1   (every error branch)

Only SILENT returns 0. The trailer `tt_capture_and_log ... run_preflight; exit $?` propagates it verbatim, so the process exit code encodes "short-circuited / did not fall through", NOT success-vs-failure. Four healthy verdicts and every error share exit 1 and are indistinguishable by status alone.

Live cron contract is SAFE and should not be changed — it keys on the verdict string, which is why this has never bitten. The trap is for any future wrapper: `set -e`, `if script; then`, `&&` chaining, or a launchd/systemd job treating non-zero as failure would skip the dispatch body on 100% of WORK ticks and log spurious failures on every LOST_ELECTION/DEFER/TOMBSTONED. Recommend either exit 0 for all non-ERROR verdicts, or an explicit comment at the trailer stating the code is not a status. Low priority, zero live impact.

It is draining docs/signals/*.json FILES and not draining signal_queue.rows[] DASHBOARD rows. So the two lanes are not equivalent and only the file lane is currently moving.

MY HOLD DECISION IS UNCHANGED, and the reasoning is now narrower and more honest: I hold because marking READ without delivery is strictly destructive (READ removes the row from po's NEW-only selector AND is terminal for orch-cold-evict), NOT because delivery is imminent. Those are different justifications and only the first one is currently supported by evidence.
